title: Selection of Expression System for Cap Protein of Porcine Circovirus as an Alternative to Baculovirus Expression System
content: Porcine circovirus type 2 (PCV2) infection is a cause of significant economic losses in swine industry. Currently swine herds are routinely vaccinated against PCV2. Commercially available vaccines for PCV2 are either inactivated vaccines or subunit vaccines that use the PCV2 capsid protein as immunogen. The recombinant capsid protein for vaccine preparations is obtained in baculovirus expression system, which is rather complicated and expensive for industrial production. Possibilities to use alternative expression systems are explored in a number of studies, but in most cases the researchers deal with one of the variants of capsid protein in a chosen setting, which makes it difficult to compare results. The current comprehensive study analyzes the production of both variants of capsid protein, full-sized and truncated, in Komagataella phaffii and Escherichia coli expression systems, under varying conditions. The expression of truncated variant reproducibly resulted in higher levels that the full-sized one. For its expression in Komagataella phaffii the maximal yield was 270 mg/L, while in Escherichia coli the yield reached 2 g/L. Both expression systems may be reasonably considered for production, but the planned comparative study of immune response to obtained proteins will give conclusive results.
